notes: Sample telegram_groups.json - the chats the bot delivers into. Copy to telegram_groups.json and edit.

'notify_level' is the routing key, and it is what builds the level -> chat map the whole toolkit sends through. Four of the names are severities (logging, warning, error, critical); the rest are streams an operator chose to separate (sql, backup, restore, sla, control). A producer asks for a level by name and the message goes wherever that name points - which is why muting a stream is done by clearing this field, not by editing code.
Two groups may not carry the same notify_level: the map has one chat per level, and the second entry would silently win.

'allow_command' is the highest command clearance this chat may exercise, checked together with the person's own user_type in telegram_users.json. Both have to allow it. A noisy logging group is usually 0 or 100 for read-only listings; a chat where somebody can restart a machine should be private, not a group.
'group_id' is negative for a group and positive for a direct message. A DM therefore cannot be declared here - put it in 'level_chat_map' in telegram_config.json instead.
'status' other than 'active' takes the chat out of routing without deleting the record of it.

telegram_groups.title: ACME DBA - Log
telegram_groups.note: Everything that ran and worked. High volume by design - it is the record, not the alarm.

telegram_groups.title: ACME DBA - Warning
telegram_groups.note: Findings that need follow-up but not tonight.

telegram_groups.title: ACME DBA - Critical
telegram_groups.note: Wakes somebody up. Keep the membership small and the threshold high, or it stops working.

telegram_groups.title: ACME DBA - Backup
telegram_groups.note: Backup and restore-drill traffic, split off so a nightly success stream does not bury a warning in the main channel.

telegram_groups.title: ACME DBA - SQL tasks
telegram_groups.note: Scheduled SQL task output and failures.
